title: MEMIT layerwise edit bank with Mirror memory coordinates
hypothesis: For fact updates whose per-layer key/value factors lie on fixed-norm two-dimensional orbits, layer-shared bases plus angle codes will store a multi-fact MEMIT-style edit bank more compactly than direct per-layer rank-one factors and generic Cartesian basis coefficients while preserving per-fact efficacy, specificity, and merged-bank interference.
physical_object: one key plane and one value plane per mediating layer (four layers)
mirror_coordinate: per-fact per-layer key and value angles; optional fact index selects each edit code
logical_multiplicity: 64 fact-specific rank-one updates distributed over four mediating layers
controls: direct MEMIT-style per-layer rank-one update factors
generic Cartesian coefficients over the same layerwise shared planes

task.orbit: per-layer unit keys and fixed-norm values lie in known 2D Givens planes

development.allowed: fixed orbit construction and exact reconstruction; no fresh result access

paid_objects: direct rank-one factors or shared per-layer key/value planes

success_gate: Every fresh world at N64: Mirror standalone efficacy NRMSE <=1e-5, specificity drift <=1e-5, serialized payload <=80% direct MEMIT-style factor bank and <=90% generic Cartesian basis; merged-bank interference differs from direct factor bank by <=1% relative.
failure_gate: Any fresh world misses quality/storage gates or Mirror merged interference differs from exact direct-factor bank by >1%; report the N-dependent frontier regardless.
boundaries: Analytic linear multi-layer MEMIT-style update-bank representation, not a learned MEMIT implementation or Transformer factual benchmark.
All layerwise edit factors are known and lie on hand-specified orbits; this is an upper-bound factor-storage screen.
Merged-bank cross-edit interference is measured as a representation-preservation audit; no claim that additive edits are semantically safe.
